newsitem.title: MEXICO: FEMSA says no to Mexico beer price war.
newsitem.headline: FEMSA says no to Mexico beer price war.

text.p: Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (FEMSA), Mexico's No. 2 brewer, on Thursday all but ruled out a price war with top beer-maker Grupo Modelo SA de CV.

"I don't think (there will be a price war) because beer prices in Mexico are very low compared to the rest of the world and I think we all want to make money," Jose Antonio Fernandez Carbajal, director general of FEMSA, told reporters.

Beverage analysts have been concerned about the future of Mexican beer prices since Modelo opened a new plant in Zacatecas state on March 14 with a capacity of 3.5 million hectoliters per year, an increase in capacity of more than 10 percent.
In an interview with Reuters at the new plant on Tuesday, Modelo's vice president of the board, Carlos Fernandez Gonzalez, said that Modelo would not initiate a price war.

Modelo, which only makes beer, holds a market-share lead over FEMSA of roughly 55 percent to 45 percent. FEMSA has other interests in soft drinks and snack foods and owns the chain of Oxxo convenience stores.

FEMSA's Fernandez Carbajal, who attended the inauguation of the Modelo plant on Monday, said he was impressed, calling it "a great investment, excellent ... a beautiful plant and a good investment for Mexico."
He also said he was unconcerned that the new Modelo plant would lead to an increase in market share for the competition.
"Having more production capacity doesn't mean anything in terms of percentage of the market," Fernandez Carbajal said. "The market is won with sales and has nothing to do with plants."
